newsitem.title: UK: LME loses battle to enforce membership - report.
newsitem.headline: LME loses battle to enforce membership - report.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange (LME) is thought to have lost its campaign to require all metal traders in London to become members of the exchange in the wake of the Sumitomo affair, the Independent newspaper said on Friday.

The LME is expected to set new information-sharing arrangements with the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) and add more independent directors to its board after a report on the affair is published, probably next week, the paper said.

Sumitomo Corp and some of the traders through which it dealt were not members of the LME when a rogue trader ran up copper losses of $2.6 billion last spring. Some copper traders are registered with the SFA, the securities market regulator.
The official report into the affair is being prepared by Britain's senior regulatory body, the Securities and Investments Board.
